question.value: Physical properties and formation of the SW molecular outflow streamer in NGC 253: gas kinematics, optical depth, dense gas fraction, and shock strength.

evidence.quote: In this work, we study the properties of the southwest (SW) outflow streamer including gas kinematics, optical depth, dense gas fraction, and shock strength through molecular emission in the central molecular zone of the starburst galaxy NGC 253.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00161.L.
In this paper, we only make use of the Band 3 data, which covers the ground-state transitions of common molecular lines that can be emitted even from the coldest ($\sim$10 K) medium.

what.value: CO(1-0) and HCN(1-0) on average optically thick in the central kpc-scale region

evidence.quote: Based on the ratios between the main and rarer isotopologues, (cite: 2015ApJ...801...63M) found that CO(1-0) and HCN(1-0) emission is on average optically thick in the central kpc-scale region of NGC 253.

what.value: Molecular and stellar bars tilt ∼18° with respect to the major axis

evidence.quote: Their studies showed that the molecular bar shares the same direction as the stellar bar in the near-infrared band, and tilts $\sim$18$^{\circ}$ with respect to the major axis (cite: 1996ApJ...470..821P; 2014A&A...567A..86I).

what.value: GMC positions and numbering 3, 6, and 7; GMC 4 identifies the second SiO ratio peak near GMC 3

what.value: GMCs can be resolved into ∼10 pc star-forming clumps

evidence.quote: The physical sizes of the three regions in Fig. [5](#fig5)(c) are $\lesssim$100 pc, which fit the scales of giant molecular clouds (GMCs), and can be further resolved into star-forming clumps ($\sim$10 pc) (cite: 2017ApJ...849...81A).

what.value: SW streamer dynamical age ∼1 Myr

evidence.quote: Given that the dynamical age of the SW streamer equaling $\sim$1 Myr is short (cite: 2017ApJ...835..265W), the star formation inside the GMCs can be the engine for the outflow streamers (cite: 2019ApJ...881...43K).

what.value: Previous HCN(1-0)/CO(1-0) peak-intensity ratio ∼1/10 in the SW streamer and starburst center

evidence.quote: (cite: 2017ApJ...835..265W) measured the ratio of peak intensities between HCN(1-0) and CO(1-0), which equals $\sim$1/10 both in the SW streamer region and the starburst center of NGC 253.

what.value: Kinetic temperature ∼100 K for excitation-density comparisons

method.value: Extract averaged CO(1-0) spectra from a beam-area circle and a high-σ ellipse; separate blueshifted streamer and redshifted disk components and derive local outflow velocity.

evidence.quote: From a circular region in the SW streamer region having the same area as the beam size (the black empty circle in Fig. [4](#fig4)b), we extract the averaged CO(1-0) spectrum
We also extract the averaged CO(1-0) spectrum from a region with high-velocity-dispersion (high-$\sigma$) in the SW streamer region (the black empty ellipse in Fig. [4](#fig4)b)

Combining the velocity field of CO(1-0) in Fig. [4](#fig4)(a), the blueshifted component relative to the reference velocity is emitted by the SW streamer, and the redshifted component is emitted by the gas disk.
The averaged CO(1-0) spectrum shows a double-peak structure, where we take the velocity $\sim$300 km s$^{-1}$ as a reference velocity for the emission near the base of the SW streamer.

assumptions.value: Use high-σ blueshifted center ∼219.7 km s−1 as the averaged streamer velocity

evidence.quote: If we take the velocity center of the blueshifted component from the high-$\sigma$ region ($\sim$219.7 km s$^{-1}$) as the averaged velocity for the SW streamer

assumptions.value: Gas-disk inclination ∼78.5°; outflow perpendicular to the disk

evidence.quote: Considering the inclination angle of the gas disk ($\sim$78.5$^{\circ}$) and the outflow being perpendicular to the disk, the deprojected local velocity of the SW streamer approaches $\sim$400 km s $^{-1}$

fitting.value: Double Gaussian fits with curve_fit; priors, bounds, likelihood, and weights not stated

evidence.quote: Using Python-based tool `curve_fit`, we fit the CO(1-0) spectra in Figs. [4](#fig4)(c) and [4](#fig4)(d) with double Gaussian function.

validation.value: Compare fitted components with the velocity field and the streamer velocity gradient in the PVD

evidence.quote: Combining the velocity field of CO(1-0) in Fig. [4](#fig4)(a), the blueshifted component relative to the reference velocity is emitted by the SW streamer, and the redshifted component is emitted by the gas disk.
Moreover, there is a gradual velocity shift along the SW streamer in the CO(1-0) PVD outlined by white dashed profiles in Fig. [3](#fig3)(a).

method.value: Map self-calibrated CO/13CO(1-0) integrated ratios and inspect ratio PVDs; compare with the literature C/13C abundance ratio.

evidence.quote: Fig. [5](#fig5)(a) shows the integrated intensity ratio map of CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) based on self-calibration, where we masked the regions with ratio S/N being less than $3\sigma$.
To decompose different velocity components, we plot in Figs. [6](#fig6)(a) and [6](#fig6)(b) the intensity ratio of CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) in the PVDs along the major axis and the SW slice

key_parameters.value: CO/13CO ratio 15 defines the disk/outflow boundary; ratio 21 outlines higher-ratio outflow regions

evidence.quote: The black contour with CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) ratio of 15 defines the boundary between the outflow streamers and the disk.
The CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) ratio further increases in part of the outflow region and is outlined by the blue contour at 21, where the CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) ratio is highest in the SW streamer region.

assumptions.value: CO/13CO ratio approaches C/13C in the optically thin limit and decreases with increasing optical depth

evidence.quote: The CO/$^{13}$CO(1-0) ratio is expected to be similar to the C/$^{13}$C isotope ratio in the optically thin limit, and decreases as the optical depth increases.
(cite: 2019A&A...624A.125M) estimated a value of the isotopic ratio C/$^{13}$C$\sim$21$\pm$6 via the integrated intensity ratio between C$^{18}$O(1-0) and $^{13}$C$^{18}$O(1-0).

assumptions.value: High kinetic temperature weakens fractionation; C and 13C can be well mixed in the outflow

evidence.quote: The molecular gas in the CMZ of NGC 253 shows high kinetic temperature in the previous studies (cite: 2004ApJ...611..835P; 2011ApJ...735...19S), which weakens the fractionation effects on C-bearing species (cite: 2020A&A...640A..51C).
Moreover, $^{13}$C preferentially forms in the center, while the C and $^{13}$C can be well mixed in the outflow region.

validation.value: Integrated-ratio maps and velocity-resolved ratios both show increased CO/13CO in the outflow

evidence.quote: Combining Figs. [5](#fig5)(a), [6](#fig6)(a), and [6](#fig6)(b), we infer that the decrease in the optical depth of CO emission happens inside the molecular outflow including the SW streamer

analysis_steps.goal: Compare dense gas along the streamer

method.value: Compare HCN/CO integrated ratios and PVD ratios with lower-opacity H13CN/13CO and N2H+/13CO diagnostics.

evidence.quote: Fig. [5](#fig5)(c) shows the integrated intensity ratio map of HCN/CO(1-0).
To confirm the distribution of the dense gas in the CMZ of NGC 253, we turn to tracers of dense gas with lower opacity.
The HCN/CO(1-0), H$^{13}$CN/$^{13}$CO(1-0) and N$_{2}$H$^{+}$/$^{13}$CO(1-0) intensity ratios in PVDs show high dense gas fraction at the base of the SW streamer.

key_parameters.value: HCN/CO sampled at -1.5″, -4″, and -6.5″ along the SW slice

evidence.quote: The orange, purple, and yellow stars in Fig. [5](#fig5)(c) mark the corresponding positions at -1.5$^{\prime\prime}$, -4$^{\prime\prime}$ and -6.5$^{\prime\prime}$ offsets from the slice center along the SW slice following (cite: 2017ApJ...835..265W).

key_parameters.value: Region A: GMC 3 near D∼0 arcsec, V∼300 km s−1; region B: streamer base at D∼[-5,0] arcsec, V∼200 km s−1

evidence.quote: One is the ellipse named region A with D$\sim$0 arcsec and V$\sim$300 km s $^{-1}$ (reference velocity) that represents the gas inside GMC 3.
The other is the ellipse named region B with D$\sim$[-5, 0] arcsec and V$\sim$200 km s$^{-1}$ (outflow velocity) that represents the gas at the base of the SW streamer.

assumptions.value: HCN/CO traces dense gas fraction; excitation-density comparison assumes ∼100 K

evidence.quote: The HCN/CO(1-0) ratio is widely used as an indicator of the fraction of dense gas, which is immediately responsible for the star formation inside galaxies (cite: 2004ApJ...606..271G; 2004ApJS..152...63G; 2012ApJ...745..190L).
The kinetic temperatures are assumed to be $\sim$100 K (cite: 2019ApJ...871..170M) in the following comparisons on the effective excitation densities between different tracers.

referee_caveats_inferred: The fitted SiO streamer peak, 0.27±0.42 mJy beam−1, is consistent with zero; its streamer-to-disk ratio is poorly constrained.
Line ratios serve as proxies; the paper does not derive absolute dense-gas fractions or fit optical depths quantitatively.
Spatial correlations and common morphology do not uniquely establish that star formation causes shocks or launches the outflow.
The ∼400 km s−1 velocity depends on the chosen reference velocity, disk inclination, and perpendicular-outflow assumption.
Detection masking can alter faint-line ratios and correlation samples; mask and uncertainty details are insufficient for exact repetition.
The numerator-intensity correlation checks the shared denominator but does not remove excitation or spatial-structure confounding.
